facets.F10_reversibility: Rollback is a three-source-file revert plus regenerated accounting/scm faces; no migrations or live state changes.
facets.F11_observability: PR evidence includes explicit local command output, review/simplification/architecture verdicts, and remote CI remains the final observable merge signal.
facets.F13_migration: Supports migration from local hardcoded gate data toward productized cloud-ci gate packets with contract-derived authority and tenant-safe false-green prevention.
facets.F1_correctness: The planning closure gate now derives the architecture rule set from specs/planning-closure-contract.json and validates masterplan/sequencing against that set; local validation reports 79 architecture rules and blocker_count=0.
facets.F2_tests: rustfmt, JSON parse, diff-check, Buck check/clippy, planning-closure validation, cross-artifact gate, registry-drift, firewall, and generated-artifact-control-plane gates passed locally before source commit; generated faces are regenerated in a settle commit.
facets.F3_maintainability: The hardcoded REQUIRED_ARCHITECTURE_RULES Rust authority is deleted; the new test uses small local normalization helpers and avoids introducing another copied rule constant.
facets.F4_compatibility: The validator accepts the current mixed representation: split required_*_rules arrays in the contract and consolidated required_rules arrays in masterplan/sequencing.
facets.F5_security: No credentials, secrets, runner permissions, or production workflow privileges are introduced; SCM facts remain the single explicit out-of-graph git boundary.
facets.F6_privacy: No tenant data, user data, or personal-data processing changes.
facets.F7_operability: Future planning-rule drift becomes a deterministic CI failure with concrete missing/extra rule diagnostics rather than a silent false-green.
facets.F8_performance: No runtime path or CI fanout expansion beyond a lightweight JSON-normalization assertion inside an existing cloud-ci gate target.
facets.F9_compliance: Records multispectrum evidence and audit-chain linkage, preserves no-new-Markdown policy, and keeps oya/dev-cli local validation as bridge evidence rather than protected-branch authority.

hyperscaler_lens.north_star: A public, hermetic, Rust cloud-ci product where CI gates consume one canonical machine-readable authority and fail closed on cross-artifact drift instead of relying on copied constants.
hyperscaler_lens.scale_property: Removing the in-code rule list collapses code/spec drift, while the cloud-ci agreement gate makes future tenant/repo adoption safer by validating generated or hand-maintained planning artifacts before merge.

known_gaps: Remote GitHub oya-ci-required/cloud-ci required context cannot be proven until after push and PR creation.

explicit_non_claims: No production deployment, tenant runtime, new external service, or protected-branch authority expansion is introduced.
No new Markdown source files are added; PR body text will be supplied from a temporary file outside the repo.
The change does not claim affected-only CI feedback can satisfy merge or phase-exit authority; remote oya-ci-required/cloud-ci remains the merge gate.
The cloud-ci test hardcodes only the canonical authority artifact paths for this repo lane; generic multi-repo packaging remains a follow-up productization layer.
scope.summary: Close a planning-closure CI false-green by making specs/planning-closure-contract.json the canonical architecture-rule source, deriving the dev-cli planning gate from that contract, and adding a hermetic cloud-ci cross-artifact agreement guard for contract/masterplan/sequencing rule drift.
